title: Conversely, the power to do good can be absent while freedom remains, as in demons, the damned and fallen man
source_text: XXXIV. Et ex adverso posse bene agere, & operari quae Deo grata sint & placeant, perfectio quaedam est, quae potest abesse ab agente libero, salva manente libertatis natura atque essentia. Quippe omnium consensu libertas in agendo mansit in daemonibus & angelis tenebrarum, nec prorsus illa perit in hominibus aeternae damnationi a Deo addictis; & tamen nec Diabolus, nec homines damnati bene agere possunt & aliquid facere quod a Deo probetur. Imo neque in hac vita homo per peccatum corruptus, & gratia Dei destitutus, quicquam praestare valet quod revera sit bonum & Deo placens. Juxta illud Domini nostri, Sine me nihil potestis facere, & consentaneum Apostoli dictum, Non quod sufficientes simus cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis: sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Et nihilominus homo induratus, & plane a Deo desertus suam in agendo libertatem retinet. Joan. 15. ver. 5. 2 Cor. 3. ver. 5.
pass_a_gloss: And on the other side to be able to act well, & to work what may be acceptable & pleasing to God, is a certain perfection, which can be absent from a free agent, the nature and essence of liberty remaining safe. Since by the consent of all liberty in acting has remained in demons & angels of darkness, nor does it altogether perish in men given over by God to eternal damnation; & yet neither the Devil, nor damned men can act well & do anything which may be approved by God. Indeed not even in this life is man corrupted by sin, & destitute of the grace of God, able to perform anything which is really good & pleasing to God. According to that of our Lord, Without me you can do nothing, & the agreeing saying of the Apostle, Not that we are sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is of God. And nevertheless man hardened, & plainly deserted by God retains his liberty in acting. John 15. ver. 5. 2 Cor. 3. ver. 5.
pass_b_english: On the other hand, being able to do good and to do what is acceptable and pleasing to God is a perfection that a free agent can lack while the nature and essence of freedom stay intact.

Everyone agrees that freedom in acting has remained in the demons, the angels of darkness, and that it does not wholly perish in men whom God has given over to eternal damnation. Yet neither the devil nor the damned can do good or do anything God approves.

Indeed, even in this life man corrupted by sin and lacking God's grace cannot achieve anything truly good and pleasing to God. As our Lord says, "Without me you can do nothing" (John 15:5), and the Apostle agrees: "Not that we are sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as from ourselves; our sufficiency is from God" (2 Corinthians 3:5). And still a man who is hardened and plainly abandoned by God keeps his freedom in acting.

choices.why: The biblical term for a heart God has given up to its sin; 'hardened' is the standard English.
